instruments.title: Rattle, made from two sheets of iron with a cane handle. The iron sheets have holes pierced in the edges, and iron loops have been threaded through in order to create the rattling sound. The handle is made from two strips of cane which have been bound together with fibre.
Banban. Slit drum made from a section of bamboo with slit cut along the length and a protruding section at top.  There is a small amount of fibre tied around the top section.

Small double head hourglass drum, made of dark brown wood, with a stepped waist. The two leather skins are laced in place with fibre strings that run the full length of the drum. There is a padded cloth ring around the edge of each skin. Some of the strings have snapped.

Kaleden. Tube zither made from a long piece of raphia palm. Strings have been formed by scraping strips from the top layer of the palm; they are held in place with fibre tied around each end of the zither.

A slit drum carved from wood, with a large handle, possibly a carved abstract head.  The slit has been roughly hewn out and there are remains of plant fibre inside.  The handle is shaped like a head with a shallow brow ridge and incised lines forming a hatched pattern where the mouth would be.

A rattle made from a curved stick which has eight serrated discs of gourd on it. The end of the stick has a small, serrated disc and is bent back towards the handle and tied off with a piece of string. A rusty iron knife is attached with a blue and tan wool, and there are also two attachments made from strips of cane.

garment.title: Rough rain hat made from splayed bark with drawn together at the crown to create a long cylindrical protrusion.

household.title: Purse made of woven plant fibre. Tubular body tied together at the base with two lengths of cotton; check weave in black and natural colours with plaited tassels at the open end.
Sling. Two lengths of equidistant twisted fibre, looped at one end, with a central curved section of approximately 14 rows.
Conical fish trap of openwork split bamboo. Tapering cylindrical single walled body with circular opening and and pointed terminus.
Bag made of string or fibre with a plaited handle attached to two sides at the opening. Bag is in two tones, neutral and black, creating a geometric pattern.
Koyupe or head band bag. Large bag woven from plant fibres with a handle formed of several plaited strips sewn together; two ply cord attached around opening to fasten.
Conical fish trap. Cylindrical single walled body, of openwork plant fibre. Access into the trap is through a partially obscured circular opening. The trap terminates into a loose point.

jewelry.title: Long necklace made from hollow seeds strung on fibre with rattling elements inside. The seeds are all of the same, scaled type and most of them are large, but there is a short section of seven significantly smaller seeds.

other.title: Scarecrow made from a long un-worked stick, attached to the top via a length of twisted plant fibre is a matt of 35 lengths of wood. At the bottom of this are seven cylindrical sticks of wood, possibly used to chime in the wind.

Leather headband with studs at regular intervals. The studs seem to be formed by folding the leather band and wrapping it with a further piece of leather to create a flat, circular stud shape. There is a fibre fastening holding the ends together.

Kose. Powder horn with conical wooden stopper. The horn has a piece of wood in the end to avoid spillage, and there is a large conical wooden stopper with resin around the edge fixing it in place.  There are small metal pins around the open edge of the horn.
Scarecrow made of a length of plaited plant fibre, tied at both ends.
